# Local review and CI receipt reuse

The canonical `skills/clouseau` skill runs Clouseau with a locally authenticated
coding harness. Installation refreshes protected public Clouseau main into one
shared user cache and registers the skill globally. Application repositories
contain their purpose and verification recipe, not copies of the review engine.

## Separate installations

Run `bash scripts/install-agent` from Clouseau, or use bastille's managed startup
bootstrap. The installer creates only a shared source cache, user-wide skill
links and the `clouseau` launcher. It creates no Actions files, provider secrets,
CI dependencies, signing credentials or branch rules. Explicit installer
`--prefix` and `--cache-root` paths support separate user profiles and isolated
installation checks without changing a home directory.

The launcher checks source freshness before every invocation. It loads an
immutable checkout for that run and preserves modified caches or unrelated
installed skills with an explicit error. An unavailable update does not silently
activate stale code. Codex and Claude Code use their existing authenticated
account stores; Clouseau makes no direct DeepSeek/Jev requests in local mode.

## Temporary directories

A run leaves no temporary directory behind. It creates `clouseau-harness-*` for a
harness call and `clouseau-wiki-index-*` for a wiki publish in the system temp
directory. It creates `clouseau-base-*`, the clean base-revision checkout used for the
`changed_lines` coverage baseline, in the work directory
`~/.local/share/clouseau/work` (inside the CLI's state directory, created with mode
0700 when missing). Each directory is removed when the step that made it ends, on
success or error, and again when the process exits or receives SIGINT, SIGTERM or
SIGHUP (exit status 128 plus the signal number). Anything that must survive a run, such
as a resumed agent exchange, lives under the state directory, never in a temporary
directory.

The base checkout lives under the home directory because the base revision's
verification runs the repository's own recipe there, and a recipe step may bind-mount
that checkout into a container with Docker Compose. Docker VMs on macOS, such as
Colima's `default` profile, share only the home directory by default. The system temp
directory (`/var/folders/...` on macOS) is not shared, so a container started against a
checkout there would see empty mounts. No extra Colima mount is needed.

At startup the launcher also removes directories that an earlier process left behind
because it was killed outright, in both the system temp directory and the work
directory: names of exactly the form `clouseau-v8-*`, `clouseau-v8-empty-*`,
`clouseau-base-*` or `clouseau-harness-*` (prefix plus the six random characters) that
are real directories (symlinks are never followed) and were last modified more than 24
hours ago. Errors are ignored. The `clouseau-v8-*` names were left by the engine's own
coverage tests, which now remove their fixtures. A `git worktree` entry whose checkout
was removed this way is pruned by `git worktree prune`.

## Local-only repository configuration

Commit `.clouseau-local.json` on the accepted base. It is independent of GitHub
Actions and contains no provider settings:

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "base_branch": "main",
  "readme": "README.md",
  "repository_policy": "AGENTS.md",
  "verification": [["npm", "run", "test:coverage"], ["npm", "run", "typecheck"]],
  "coverage": {
    "format": "istanbul",
    "report": "coverage/coverage-final.json",
    "source_directory": "src"
  }
}
```

`llvm` and `lcov` (production sources only; `DA` lines and `BRDA` branches) are also supported. A version 2 `lcov` part may add
`source_suffixes` (for example `[".swift"]`, see [changed-line coverage](changed-line-coverage.md#swift-rust-and-other-lcov-languages)) to cover
a non-JS/TS language. The shared parser requires complete, nonempty exact
line/branch counters. Commands run as argument arrays, without shell expansion.
The accepted base supplies the recipe; a change cannot weaken its own checks.
The source checkout must be committed and clean before review. Verification
artifacts should use the repository's established ignored output locations.

### Multiple native coverage artifacts

Version 2 keeps separate native reports for applications with multiple source
roots. Its `coverage` field is a nonempty array with at most 32 explicit parts:

```json
{
  "version": 2,
  "base_branch": "main",
  "readme": "README.md",
  "repository_policy": "AGENTS.md",
  "verification": [
    ["python3", "-m", "coverage", "run", "--branch", "--source", "backend", "-m", "unittest", "discover", "-s", "backend/tests"],
    ["python3", "-m", "coverage", "json", "-o", "coverage/backend.json"],
    ["npm", "--prefix", "frontend", "run", "test:coverage"]
  ],
  "coverage": [
    {"format": "coveragepy", "report": "coverage/backend.json", "source_directory": "backend"},
    {"format": "istanbul", "report": "frontend/coverage/coverage-final.json", "source_directory": "frontend/app"}
  ]
}
```

Only the six documented top-level fields are accepted in version 2: `version`,
`base_branch`, `readme`, `repository_policy`, `verification`, and `coverage`, plus the documented optional fields
(`OPTIONAL_LOCAL_KEYS` in `src/coverage-plan.cjs`): today only [`review_reuse`](#reusing-answers-in-clouseau-review-opt-in),
which both versions accept. Every reader of the file checks against that one list: `readLocalConfig` (local review,
refresh and installation), `coverageParts` (strict in CI's attestation, lenient locally) and the coverage gate's own recipe
reader, which `plan`, `totals-plan`, `changed-plan` and `declared-plan` use on the base branch's file in consumer CI.
Misspelled or additional policy fields fail before local command execution and at the CI data entrypoint (the gate says
`Unknown version 2 coverage recipe field`). Each coverage part likewise accepts only its three
documented fields, plus the optional `package_directory` that only [declared coverage](declared-coverage.md#monorepos-one-declaration-per-part) reads and, for `lcov` parts only, the optional `source_suffixes` list. Version 1 keeps its existing compatibility behavior.

Adapt commands to the repository's real test suite. The runner passes argument
arrays directly, runs every command, and checks each untouched native report.
It does not generate a combined artifact or reinterpret counters. Native
measurement requires a complete application inventory and nonempty measured
lines. Local AI review records valid partial counts and unavailable, invalid or
unverified coverage honestly, then runs regardless of the percentage. It does
not label an old artifact as this run's verified coverage. CI's separate exact
coverage gate still requires 100% lines and branches for every part (unless the protected configuration opts in to [changed-line](changed-line-coverage.md) or [declared](declared-coverage.md) coverage; local status stays advisory exact either way). A genuinely
branchless part may have zero branches when another part supplies measured
branches; an entirely branchless plan fails that CI gate. One part cannot
compensate for another part's missing or uncovered data.

Report and source paths must be repository-relative. Resolved source roots must
exist and must not overlap, and report paths must be unique, including aliases.
Both recipe versions accept `source_directory: "."` for the complete repository
root, including executable root configuration and nested application sources.
A version 2 root part cannot appear alongside another part because their source
roots overlap. The canonical `.` spelling is allowed only for a source directory;
report and other paths keep their existing restrictions. A root recipe still
rejects missing native source measurements and uncovered counters.
Paths that escape the checkout fail. There is no arbitrary exclusion option.
Generated application code, executable configuration and entry points remain
in scope. Native JS/TS inventory excludes declaration-only `.d.ts` files,
`*.test.*`/`*.spec.*` files and the fixed `test`, `tests`, `__tests__`, `.git`,
`node_modules` and `vendor` directories. Native coverage.py uses its documented
Python test/dependency conventions. Those non-application entries may appear in
a native report but cannot contribute passing counters.

Version 2 supports native measurement through the complete-inventory `istanbul`,
`coveragepy`, `go` and `lcov` adapters. Version 1's single-report interface, including LLVM,
remains supported. Unsupported native formats are reported as unavailable local
coverage; they do not suppress AI review or acquire invented counters. CI still
rejects unsupported formats. LLVM multi-root plans require a complete
compiled-source inventory capability and are not measured by version 2.
Go is measured only through the `go` adapter, whose lines are statements and
branches are basic blocks ([native Go coverage](go-coverage.md)).

The accepted base supplies the complete recipe in normal local review. Local
evidence records actual command outcomes, the digest of each command's complete stdout
and stderr and their tails (the last 128 characters of a command that succeeded, the last
4,096 of one that failed, with `stdout_bytes`/`stderr_bytes` stating the full length wherever a stream was cut), native counters when valid,
artifact digests and freshness, unavailable-coverage diagnostics, and the accepted
configuration digest. A nonzero command is not assumed to have failed only
because of coverage. One frozen engine checks every part throughout the review.

CI invokes the same shared verifier through `operation: coverage` with
`coverage-config`. That input accepts only a **version 2** recipe: a version 1
file fails with `Coverage gate failed: A multi-artifact coverage recipe requires
version 2`. A repository whose CI uses `coverage-config` therefore commits
`.clouseau-local.json` as version 2 with a one-element `coverage` array (the
version 1 example above is for local-only use or for the legacy
`coverage-report` + `source-directory` inputs). Supply the recipe from the exact accepted base, separately
from the candidate checkout. For example, in an unprivileged PR verification
job with no provider credentials:

```yaml
- uses: actions/checkout@v4
  with:
    ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
    fetch-depth: 0
- name: Read accepted coverage recipe
  env:
    BASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
  run: git show "$BASE_SHA:.clouseau-local.json" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/accepted-coverage.json"
# Run the repository's actual tests and native instrumentation here.
- uses: gaulatti/clouseau@FULL_REVIEWED_COMMIT_SHA
  with:
    operation: coverage
    coverage-config: ${{ runner.temp }}/accepted-coverage.json
```

The coverage action reads that JSON as data and never executes its verification
commands. Do not supply proposed PR policy as the accepted recipe. Configuration
selection belongs to trusted workflow wiring; source execution, credentialed
assessment and the write-capable controller remain separate. `coverage-config`
cannot be combined with legacy `coverage-report` or `source-directory` inputs.
The legacy single-report inputs are unchanged.

Store the requirement outside the checkout, then run:

```bash
clouseau review --directory /path/to/repository --base origin/main \
  --request-file /path/to/requirement.txt --harness codex
```

Verification subprocesses and the native coverage parser receive the same
credential-filtered environment as initial installation: inherited variable names
matching `KEY`, `TOKEN`, `SECRET`, `PASSWORD` or `CREDENTIAL` are removed.
Nonsecret runtime and tooling variables remain available. Repository verification
commands supply their own nonproduction fixture configuration. PEM private-key
output is rejected before it can enter AI evidence.

### Agent-driven review inside an AI harness

The headless `--harness codex|claude` form launches a separate child process per
model session. It is for a person at a plain terminal. Inside Claude Code, Codex
or opencode the calling agent supplies those sessions itself:

```bash
clouseau review --directory /path/to/repository --base origin/main \
  --request-file /path/to/requirement.txt --agent opencode
```

`--agent` accepts `claude`, `codex` or `opencode` and excludes `--harness`.
The controller still owns real verification, immutable sources, citations, grading
formulas, the finding ledger and the decision. When it needs a model session it
writes `request-NNNN.json`, the full `prompt-NNNN.txt` and `schema-NNNN.json` under
the review cache's `agent/` directory (outside the checkout), prints
`status: awaiting_agent` and exits with code 3. The agent starts a fresh subagent
or session that sees only those files, has it write a JSON answer to the request's
`answer_file`, and registers it:

```bash
clouseau respond --agent-request REQUEST_FILE --answer ANSWER_FILE --session SESSION_ID
```

The `awaiting_agent` output already prints this command with a valid, unused session identifier in place of
`SESSION_ID`, and a `session_rule` field that states the rule: 8 to 128 characters, letters, digits and `. _ : -`
only, starting with a letter or digit, never reused for another request. Any identifier that satisfies the rule may
replace the suggested one.

`prompt-NNNN.txt` is the policy text followed by the evidence, laid out over many lines instead of one line of up to hundreds of
kilobytes. The layout is applied only when printing the parsed evidence compactly gives back the original bytes exactly (so no
number or string is altered); otherwise the file is the original prompt. The request digest, the reuse key and answer
validation always use the original prompt, never the file.

The schema file is compact JSON Schema that states each repeated subschema (chiefly the
proof-ID enumeration every citation site shares) once under `$defs` and points at it with
`"$ref": "#/$defs/NAME"`; it is the same constraint as the full inline schema, a few KB
instead of hundreds. `respond` validates the answer against the request schema (the
supported subset, with only those `$defs` references, fails closed on unknown keywords), refuses a session identifier already used for
another request in the exchange, and allows three attempts per request. A rejected answer's reason is passed to the next
attempt. When an examiner or challenger drops or rewords a concern from its own earlier draft, the reason names that finding.
For a restatement under the same identifier, it also names the first field that differs (cause or obligation) and quotes the
earlier text, so the next fresh session can retain it verbatim or resolve it with current-source counterevidence. Repeating
the identical `review` command then resumes: it reuses the one recorded
verification, requires the same frozen evidence digest, replays accepted answers
and stops at the next pending session. A request whose stored digest no longer
matches stops the review rather than guessing.

An in-flight agent review is pinned to the engine revision that started it. The
launcher still refreshes protected main before every call, but a continuation of the
same head, base and requirement re-executes the recorded revision from the local
cache (`~/.cache/clouseau/revisions/<sha>`; the installer never prunes revisions, and
a pin under `~/.local/share/clouseau/pins/` is the reference that names one) and
prints one line stating the pinned revision and the newer one, once per newer revision (the pin remembers that it said so; a
still newer revision is announced again). The pinned checkout
must be an unmodified worktree of the installer's own cached source whose engine
digest equals the one recorded when the pin was made; otherwise the command fails and
nothing from it runs. A receipt is issued under the pinned revision, so CI, which
ignores a receipt whose engine differs from protected main, reviews the PR itself.
A new review (different head or requirement) uses the newest revision. Pass
`--engine latest` to drop the pin and restart on the newest revision; the pin is also
released when the review completes. A failure of the pinned engine is reported with the engine's own error message (its last 2,000
characters), not a bare exit status. `respond` needs no pinning: it validates against
the schema stored with the request.

Usage records for these sessions carry `harness` (`claude`, `codex` or `opencode`),
`execution: agent_session`, the supplied session identifier and digests of the
request, answer and stored response file. Receipt validation accepts them alongside
headless records and still requires distinct sessions for the examiner and
challenger investigation and grading phases. The controller cannot itself prove
that a subagent was isolated from the implementer, so this independence rests on
the runner's trust boundary and on the enrolled engine revision: CI accepts a
receipt only from a Clouseau revision the protected configuration enrolls, which is
where an owner decides whether to trust agent-driven receipts. The signed handoff,
`independent_ci_required` and `merge_authority: false` are unchanged.

Outside an AI harness, use `--harness claude` to run Claude Code headlessly. The controller runs real verification,
records its actual outcomes, captures immutable base/head sources and accepted
purpose, and starts separate examiner and challenger sessions. Coverage below
100%, a failing coverage command, or unavailable, malformed or unsupported
coverage does not prevent those local AI sessions. Additional source requests are bounded. Fresh
semantic grading sessions supply descriptive factor levels; the same Clouseau
code owns citations, formulas, thresholds and final decisions. No investigator
gets the implementer's conversation or the other investigator's conclusions.

The controller identifies this as a pre-PR assessment in both investigation and
grading. It requires the accepted local recipe, safe complete immutable source
and meaningful evidence for the changed behavior. Coverage percentage or
unavailable coverage alone does not force a failing AI quality verdict; actual
behavioral defects, deceptive tests and missing material evidence still do. The
review never rewrites failed or unavailable verification into a test pass.

New and cached CLI results identify `decision_scope: review_reuse_only`,
`independent_ci_required: true` and `merge_authority: false`, with local
verification and coverage status separate from the AI decision. A local
`auto_approve` verdict means passing AI quality evidence eligible for signed
reuse, not technical approval. CI audit, workflow and container execution remains
independent; a local receipt does not claim those results or authorize GitHub
approval. CI must pass every mandatory technical gate before approval or merge.

A source-line reference can be normalized only to an existing immutable catalog
block containing that line. The controller preserves the observation and reads
the literal source bytes; this correction needs no additional model request.
Unknown sources, out-of-range lines and unsupplied blocks still stop review.

Reports and response journals stay outside source control. A completed identical
input is not automatically reviewed again. Fix blocking findings, commit the
changed implementation and reassess. A negative or incomplete review never
produces an approval receipt. This initial receipt path targets a new PR without
an unresolved existing GitHub review ledger; it rejects an existing incompatible
ledger rather than dropping its findings.

## Receipt-attested verification

A receipt signed by an enrolled identity attests the repository's whole declared verification. `clouseau review` runs every command of the
accepted base `.clouseau-local.json` (plus any `--additional-checks`) and, **before spending any AI review, refuses to sign** (non-zero exit,
no receipt, no marker) unless all of the following hold on the exact head:

- every command ran and exited 0 (a tool that is not installed, such as `cargo llvm-cov` or `coverage.py`, is a refusal that names the
  command and the missing tool, never a partial signature);
- native coverage was produced by this run;
- the coverage gate CI enforces passes: exact 100%, or for the protected `coverage.mode` of `changed_lines` the changed lines and branches are
  covered with no repository-wide regression (the base revision is measured locally in a temporary clean worktree, as CI measures it), or
  for `declared` the minimums declared at the base.

Declare every check you want skipped in CI (tests, coverage, fmt, lint, frontend, infrastructure) as a command of `.clouseau-local.json`.
Without an enrolled identity nothing is signed and the review remains advisory. The signed verification record then carries
`attestation: {version, recipe, commands, coverage_mode, gate: "passed"}`; receipts issued before this change carry none, stay valid for the
AI review, and attest no verification.

In CI, `operation: attested` (inputs `config`, `github-token`; output `attested`) answers `'true'` only when the pull request's receipt passes
every check the assessment applies (signature, enrolled key and author, expiry, exact head and base, engine, signed sources against live
GitHub; under the protected `binding: "diff"` the normalized diff and the live base's recipe instead of the head, base and sources, see
[binding a receipt to its diff](#binding-a-receipt-to-its-diff-opt-in)) AND attests the accepted base recipe. Anything else (no marker,
expired, wrong head without that binding, old receipt, an error) is `'false'`. Gate any
workflow on it in a small job, as `examples/consumer-ci.yml` does:

```yaml
if: needs.attested.outputs.attested != 'true'   # on each test step, or on a whole job in another workflow
```

The skip is advisory; the enforcement is in the engine. When the configured `verification.job` succeeds with required steps `skipped`,
the engine accepts them only after verifying the same receipt itself in the trusted workflow; without a valid attesting receipt a skipped
required step is the failure it always was. A receipt expires (`max_age_seconds`), so re-run the workflow after expiry and the checks run;
the failure then names the receipt class (`receipt_expired` with its expiry instant) and that step, or `clouseau refresh --pr N` to renew
the receipt ([notices](notices.md#skipped-verification-step-without-an-attesting-receipt)).
The job named in `verification.job` must still exist and succeed, so keep it as a job whose steps are skipped rather than removing it.

## Evidence size

The review cache's `snapshot.json`, the `record` output and the signed `receipt.json` are
written as compact JSON, without indentation (about 15% of a typical receipt); they parse
identically and the published artifact was already compact.

Serialized local evidence is capped at 900,000 characters. To keep large changes inside the cap
without dropping anything a reviewer judges, the local collector stores a file added whole once:
its snapshot entry keeps the patch header and `patch_body: "head_source"`, the body being exactly
the head source with every line prefixed `+` (consumers restore the identical patch). The pinned
engine seed (roughly 380 KB) is collected only when a workflow change adds or changes a
`gaulatti/clouseau/scripts/resolve@main` (or an existing `@<sha>`) reference; an ordinary edit of a workflow that keeps its reference
carries no engine source, and a reviewer can still request any of it. The seed is optional context: seed files that would use the last 150,000
characters are listed in `omitted_sources` with a reason, and reviewers can still request them.
A source a reviewer requests that would take the evidence past the 900,000-character budget is omitted the same way, with
the hosted review's reason `would exceed the total evidence budget` (one rule for both, `admitWithinBudget` in
`src/acceptance-sources.cjs`); the rest of the request is still read and the review continues. A reviewer that then records
the omitted source as missing evidence leaves review completeness unresolved, and CI refuses such a receipt
(`receipt_completeness`). A change near the budget whose reviewers need large context is therefore signed only once it is
split into smaller pull requests, or reviewed by a chunked scheme that supplies that context.
Changed files, their base and head sources and contracts are never omitted; a change that exceeds
the cap with only that evidence is reviewed in bounded units (see "Chunked local review") unless the protected configuration disabled chunked review, in which case it fails closed.

## Enrolling a trusted runner

Consumers with neither accepted recipe nor CI policy use the separate
[explicit initial trust installation](initial-installation.md). Its frozen
owner/admin commit-comment grant and installation-only evidence cannot replace
ordinary approval or authorize automatic merge.

`clouseau init-identity` creates an Ed25519 identity outside the repository with
private file permissions. Its output contains only the public enrollment entry
and local identity-file path. Identity creation is explicit and is never part of
agent installation. The existing authenticated GitHub account supplies the
identity's `github_actor`.

An owner must install the public enrollment entry in protected CI configuration:

```json
{
  "local_review": {
    "mode": "required",
    "central_source": {"repository": "gaulatti/clouseau", "ref": "refs/heads/main"},
    "max_age_seconds": 172800,
    "keys": [{
      "id": "PUBLIC_KEY_IDENTIFIER",
      "issuer": "ENROLLED_RUNNER_IDENTIFIER",
      "github_actor": "ENROLLED_GITHUB_LOGIN",
      "public_key": "ED25519_PUBLIC_PEM",
      "revoked": false
    }]
  }
}
```

This source authorization requires the [automatic CI resolver wiring](automatic-ci-upgrades.md)
and its frozen SHA/digest; configuration alone cannot select an engine. Legacy
fixed installations instead enroll `reviewer_digest` and omit `central_source`.
The modes are exclusive, and only the central-source integration avoids recurring
release enrollment PRs.

Receipt lifetime: `issueReceipt` defaults to 48 hours (172800 seconds), and the
trust validator rejects `max_age_seconds` above 172800. Each consumer sets its
own `max_age_seconds` in its protected `.github/clouseau.json`; the example
configuration uses 172800, and consumers that still say 3600 keep one-hour
receipts until raised separately. A receipt that expires after CI skipped the
tests on its strength fails the skipped step, naming `receipt_expired` (see above). The first
[initial-installation](initial-installation.md) authorization deliberately stays
at one hour, and installation receipts are capped by it. A receipt remains bound
to the exact head SHA (or, under the protected `binding: "diff"`, to its
normalized diff), signed review history and reviewer digest, so a changed head
(or diff) invalidates it regardless of age.

Only existing protected configuration can enroll or revoke a key. A contributor
cannot authorize their own key through the proposed PR. Keys are restricted to
their enrolled native GitHub PR author. Set `revoked` or remove a key to reject
its future receipts. `optional` mode permits the separately installed CI AI
reviewer for PRs without a receipt, and for any receipt that does not verify (it is
ignored, see below). `required` mode needs no CI AI provider credentials.

Malformed, unknown-version, duplicate or mixed receipt marker claims are ignored
before any artifact is fetched, with the `malformed` notice: in `optional` mode CI
reviews the change itself, in `required` mode the outcome is `local_receipt_required`.
Do not normalize an invalid stamp; replace it with a fresh receipt.

The initial trust boundary is an enrolled maintainer workstation, including its
operator and privileged processes. The identity is not remote or hardware
attestation. A private key held by that operating-system account cannot protect
against malicious processes with equivalent account access. Such a compromise
can forge the runner's claims. Signatures protect receipt integrity and identify
the enrolled issuer; they do not mathematically prove that an LLM executed or
that its conclusions are correct. Stronger hostile-runner protection requires
an independently isolated execution/signing service and is not claimed here.

## Signed handoff

An enrolled runner selects its matching installed identity automatically. Use
`--identity /path/to/identity.json` to select explicitly when needed. The runner
requires an unmodified public Clouseau engine and the enrolled signer. CI
authorizes the exact engine separately from the signature. Legacy CI without a
trusted frozen-source selection still requires its configured digest. It records the exact Clouseau commit and binds the executable engine,
skill, scripts and policy by a SHA-256 content digest. Legacy fixed-digest installations permit identical engine content across squash
identities. [Automatic CI upgrades](automatic-ci-upgrades.md) require both the
exact selected central commit and its computed digest; no cross-version
compatibility is inferred. It verifies
the same source and installation remain unchanged before
issuing a passing receipt. Signing material is never placed in model packets,
child-process environments, project source, reports or the published artifact.
Protected review-control changes still require the separate owner-authorized
installation path; a local receipt cannot grant that authority. A current-head owner confirmation
is independently recorded and revalidated by CI when a signed review accompanies
a review-control change.

The receipt signs a domain-separated SHA-256 payload with Ed25519. It includes
the complete review record, exact repository/head/base, Clouseau and policy/config
identities, issuer/key, issuance/expiry, and a 256-bit random nonce. Publish it
before opening the PR:

```bash
clouseau publish --directory /path/to/repository --receipt /path/to/receipt.json
```

This creates a separate artifact commit and unique `clouseau-review/<nonce>` tag;
it does not change the reviewed source commit or checkout. Include the returned
`clouseau-local-review:v1` marker in the initial ready PR body. The complete
artifact follows the repository's visibility and contains reviewed source and
the requirement text; those inputs must be appropriate for publication there.

## Refreshing a pull request after its base moved

Every merge to the base leaves the other open pull requests behind it: GitHub reports `branch update needed`, and each
assessment and approval is bound to the old base, as is each receipt unless the protected `binding: "diff"` binds it to its
diff instead ([binding a receipt to its diff](#binding-a-receipt-to-its-diff-opt-in)). `clouseau refresh` does the author's manual routine for one
pull request, in the pull request's own checkout:

```bash
clouseau refresh --pr N --agent claude                       # inside an AI harness
clouseau refresh --pr N --harness claude                     # headless
clouseau refresh --pr N --request-file req.txt --agent claude   # an explicit requirement
```

`--request-file` is optional. Without it the requirement is the one of the last accepted (`auto_approve`) review of this
repository and branch: every accepted review stores its requirement text byte for byte as `request.txt` beside its record under
`~/.local/share/clouseau/reviews/<cache id>/`, with a `requirement.json` that binds it, and one pointer per repository and
branch (`requirements/`) names the newest. The command refuses, and asks for `--request-file`, when nothing is recorded for the
branch, when the record is unusable (pointer and record name different repositories, branches, heads or cache ids; the text no
longer hashes to the recorded digest; a part is a link, empty or over 20,000 characters), when the recorded head is not an
ancestor of the pull request head, or is already in the base (the branch name was reused after another pull request merged), or when that review also used
`--additional-checks` (they are part of its input and are not stored; pass both again). It never guesses among candidates.
Optional: `--directory`, `--identity`, `--additional-checks`, `--engine latest`. In order, and never otherwise:

1. refuse (see below), then `git fetch origin <base>`; if the pull request already contains the base tip, the receipt in the
   pull request body decides: one that still verifies for this head ends the command with `up_to_date`, any other is
   [renewed](#renewing-a-receipt-that-no-longer-verifies) (steps 3 to 5 below, no merge and no push of the branch). Under the
   protected `binding: "diff"`, when the pull request does not contain the base tip and its receipt still covers its diff, the
   base is merged and the normalized diff recomputed; if it is unchanged the merge is pushed with no review and the command
   ends with `updated` (see [Binding a receipt to its diff](#binding-a-receipt-to-its-diff-opt-in)); otherwise the steps
   continue on that merge;
2. check with `git merge-tree` that the merge is clean, then **merge** the base (`git merge --no-ff`, message
   `Merge origin/<base> into <branch>`). There is no rebase and no force-push anywhere in the command;
3. run the ordinary local review of the head (`clouseau review`, including its verification) with the answers reused as
   described below, and sign the receipt. The claimed title of the change is the pull request's own title (GitHub's), not the
   subject of the merge commit, which is only `Merge origin/<base> into <branch>`; a pull request with no title is refused;
4. `clouseau publish` the receipt (this pushes only the artifact tag `clouseau-review/<nonce>`);
5. replace the `clouseau-local-review:v1` marker in the pull request body (appended when there is none);
6. `git push origin HEAD:<pull request branch>`, once, as the last step.

It refuses, with a message that names the cause and before pushing anything, when: the worktree has uncommitted or untracked
changes; HEAD is not the head GitHub reports for the pull request (when the local branch only has commits on top of that head, the message
says how many are unpushed and that you must `git push` first, then refresh again); the pull request is closed, comes from a fork, is not the
checked-out branch, or is not against the configured `base_branch`; the harness is unknown or its program is not installed;
the base conflicts with the branch (the checkout is left untouched and the conflicting paths are listed); a hook refuses the
merge (it is aborted). It never pushes when the review does not pass (`repair_required`, `review_incomplete`, ...), when a
passing review produced no signed receipt (no enrolled identity), when the checkout changed during the review, when the
pull request closed or got another head during the review, or when the push is rejected (the body is then restored). After
a review that does not pass, the merge commit stays in the local branch: repair, commit and refresh again, or run `git reset
--hard <old head>` to discard it. An agent-driven refresh that returns `awaiting_agent` is repeated with the identical
command; it recognises its own merge commit (the pull request head and a commit of the base as parents), does not merge or
fetch again, and continues on the base it began with. While Clouseau main advances, the continuation runs on the engine revision
that started the exchange ([pinning](#agent-driven-review-inside-an-ai-harness)): through the `clouseau` launcher the pinned engine
receives your own `refresh` command, resumes it and finishes it (review, publication, marker, push), and its result is what you
see. If the pinned engine fails, its error message is shown.

### Binding a receipt to its diff (opt-in)

By default a receipt is bound to the exact head and base commits it reviewed, so every merge to the base voids the receipt of
every other open pull request. With the protected `local_review.binding: "diff"` in `.github/clouseau.json` on the base branch,
a receipt is bound to the **change** instead: it covers a pull request when the SHA-256 of the pull request's normalized diff
equals the SHA-256 of the normalized diff in the signed record (`src/receipt-patch.cjs`). The receipt format does not change:
the signed record already carries every patch.

The normalized diff is, per changed file in path order, its path, its status and (for a rename) its previous path, and its
hunks with every hunk header reduced to `@@`, so line numbers and git's trailing section text do not count. Every other byte
of a hunk counts, context lines and whitespace included. GitHub joins two git hunks that are one unchanged line apart; that
run of exactly seven context lines between two changes is split back into its two hunks on both sides. A summarized lockfile
contributes its path and status, and its derived summary is recomputed from the live lockfile bytes and must equal the signed
one apart from the revision it names.

| | Binding absent | `binding: "diff"` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| a different head commit (GitHub's branch update, a merge of the base) | `receipt_revision_head` | covered while the diff is unchanged |
| a different base commit | `receipt_revision_base` | covered while the diff is unchanged |
| signed full-file sources compared with the live repository | compared | not compared: the signed record is what was reviewed; each source must still name a signed revision |
| the repository's contracts (`readme`, `repository_policy`, for example `.github/clouseau.md` and `README.md`) | compared at the signed base, which must be the live base | compared at the **live** base: a base move that changed either voids the receipt (`receipt_source`, naming the file) |
| lines added above a hunk on the base | `receipt_source` | covered |
| any change to an added, removed or context line, or to whitespace | `receipt_source` | `receipt_source`, naming the file |
| a file added, removed or re-statused, another rename | refused | refused, unchanged |
| a compatibility declaration (`compat/declarations/<sha256>.json`) declared again after a merge | refused (its bytes changed) | covered while every declaration keeps its verdict over the same files (path, mode, deleted or not); only the content digests it pins may differ |
| a file without a GitHub patch | refused, unless the live sources prove it shows no text | refused, even an empty file or an identical rename: the live sources are not read |
| signature, enrolled key, author, expiry, repository, protected configuration and policy digests, engine and review semantics, passing decision | bound | bound, unchanged |

A compatibility declaration ([receipt compatibility](receipt-compatibility.md)) pins the full content of the semantic files
it covers. When the base gains a merged pull request that changed one of those files, merging the base makes the
declaration stale, and declaring again replaces it with a new file under a new name. Under the binding that replacement does
not void the receipt: a file added under exactly `compat/declarations/<64 hex>.json` whose whole content is a well-formed
declaration is compared by what it declares, its verdict (`compatible` or `incompatible`) and the files it covers with their
mode and whether each is deleted, and it is left out of the normalized diff. A changed verdict, a file added to or removed
from a declaration, or a declaration gained or lost voids the receipt (`receipt_source`). Any other file under that directory
(another name, another status, a body that is not one whole declaration) is an ordinary changed file. The required `verify`
job still checks every declaration against the merged tree, so a declaration whose digests do not match the code fails
there. The pull request's changed-file count still includes the declarations.

**What still voids a diff-bound receipt after a base move.** A change on the base branch to the repository's contracts
(`readme` and `repository_policy`, compared at the live base) or to the declared recipe (`.clouseau-local.json`, which the
test waiver compares at the live base) voids every open diff-bound receipt, by design: the change was judged against them. A
summarized lockfile's summary is recomputed from the live base and head lockfile bytes, so a base move that changed a
lockfile the pull request also changes voids it when the recomputed summary differs.

The test waiver follows the same binding: `operation: attested` answers `'true'` for a receipt whose diff matches and whose
signed `.clouseau-local.json` equals the live base's, so the tests are **not** rerun after a base move or an update-branch
merge. This is deliberate and has a cost: a break caused only by the base move (a semantic conflict between the reviewed change
and the new base) is found after merge, by the next run on the base. **Accepted limit:** no CI step reruns the attested tests
of a diff-bound receipt for any base move, including one that changed a file the pull request imports or calls but does not
edit; only a change to the declared recipe (`.clouseau-local.json`) or to the pull request's own diff makes CI run them. The run-consistency checks that compare the live pull
request between the assessment and the gate are unchanged; they protect one CI run from a push that lands mid-run.

`clouseau refresh` uses the same decision: under the binding it judges the receipt (including the diff, from the files GitHub
lists) before merging anything. When it stands, refresh merges the base locally and recomputes the normalized diff: if it
equals the diff before the merge (the base moved elsewhere, or on lines of a changed file outside every hunk), refresh pushes
the merge (a plain push, never forced) with no review and no new receipt, and answers `updated`. That keeps the branch strictly
ahead of the base, which the controller-managed merge requires. Only when the merge changed the diff (the base moved a line
inside a hunk's context) does refresh review the merged head, as it does without the binding. On an up-to-date branch it answers `up_to_date` whenever CI would accept the receipt. Who
updates the branch is therefore the author: by `clouseau refresh`, by GitHub's "Update branch" (`gh pr update-branch`), or by a
plain merge and push; the workflow token cannot, because its push starts no verification. A merge commit that leaves the
diff unchanged keeps the receipt valid end to end, at the assessment and at the gate (`verifyRecord`, and `verifySources` at
the gate's write boundary), which `src/acceptance-controller-binding.test.cjs` proves through an assessment and gate approval
of the merged head with zero AI calls. A receipt that no longer covers the diff is refreshed or renewed as usual.

`updated` never pushes a head that fails a cheap deterministic invariant of the repository; it does not run the verification
recipe. In a repository with compatibility declarations (a `compat/manifest.json` and a `compat/declarations/` directory,
as in Clouseau's own; see [receipt compatibility](receipt-compatibility.md#declare-then-fold)), refresh checks the merged tree
with the same `inspect` as `scripts/review-compatibility verify` before the push. When the merge only changed a file the pull
request declared, so its declaration pins stale content, and the stale declarations cover exactly the pull request's own
changed semantic files with one decision, refresh replaces them with one declaration of that decision over the same files,
commits it as `chore(compat): re-pin the compatibility declaration after merging origin/<base>` and pushes both commits; the
result then carries `declaration: "re-pinned"`. Any other finding (a different path set, an undeclared change, mixed
decisions, or a base change to a declared file that is not folded yet) pushes nothing and names the cause; the merge commit
stays in the local branch. A repository without that tooling is refreshed exactly as before.

The owner's `/approve-intent` (and an approving review) names one exact head, under the binding too, unless the protected
`local_review.confirmation: "diff"` is set as well (it is valid only together with `binding: "diff"`). With it, a
confirmation of an earlier head (comment or approving review) also counts for the current head when that earlier commit was
this pull request's: an ancestor of the head, or, after a rebase, a commit that one of the pull request's force pushes
replaced or produced or an ancestor of one. The engine reads those force pushes itself from the pull request's timeline
(`HeadRefForcePushedEvent`), never from comment text; more than 100 force pushes, or a commit GitHub no longer has, does
not carry. In addition, its normalized diff (taken from its merge base with the live base) equals the pull request's
current diff, and its merge base carries the same `.github/clouseau.json` and purpose contract (`repository_policy`) as the
live base. A merge of the base or a rebase onto it that leaves the change unchanged therefore keeps the confirmation; any push
that changes the diff (a new commit, or a conflict resolution that alters the branch's own lines), and any base change to
the protected configuration or the contract, voids it. A base change that edits the lines around the branch's own change
changes the diff's context lines, so it voids the confirmation too; a change elsewhere in the same file only moves the
hunk offsets, which the normalized diff ignores. A patchless or truncated file list, an
unknown commit or another lineage never matches, and any other API failure surfaces. The comment itself stays exactly
`/approve-intent <sha>`. The recorded authorization names the head it was applied to and, when that differs, the
`confirmed_sha` it was given for. Without the setting, a confirmation names the exact head, as before. Where the binding applies: `verifySignedRecord` (the head and base comparison),
`verifySources` (revisions, sources, contract and verification refs, the lockfile summary, and the diff through `verifyPatches`),
and through them `screenReceipt`, `screenSources`, `receiptAttests`, `rehydrate` and `verifyRecord` (the record's revisions), and
`receipt-standing.cjs` and `pr-refresh.cjs`. An installation receipt is never diff-bound.

When a confirmation of an earlier head carries under `confirmation: "diff"`:

| Change since the confirmed head | Confirmation |
| --- | --- |
| a merge of the base, or a rebase onto it, that leaves the pull request's diff unchanged | carries |
| a base change elsewhere in a changed file (only the hunk offsets move) | carries |
| a re-declaration of compatibility (`compat/declarations/`) after a base merge that keeps every verdict over the same files and only re-pins content hashes | carries, exactly as the receipt binding treats it (`splitDeclarations` in `src/receipt-patch.cjs`, the one rule both use) |
| a declaration whose verdict changed, a newly declared file, or a declaration added or removed | voids it |
| a new commit, or a conflict resolution that alters the branch's own lines | voids it |
| a base change to the lines around the branch's change, to `.github/clouseau.json` or to the purpose contract | voids it |
| a patchless or truncated file list, an unknown commit or another lineage | voids it |
